# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration
scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable —
field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a
live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and
game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up
level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped
(`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the
shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB,
AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it**
the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms
(`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels;
the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a
*minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up
(P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer
cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification**
(no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can
  collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change,
  so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real
  gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every
  power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be
  applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is
  auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level
  curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up
  repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene
  shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all
  catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the
  shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`);
  it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and
  introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body
  guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`
  drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling,
  hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade /
  mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run
  restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside
  `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep
  (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable
  effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7
  teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the
  shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body
  guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up
  leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests
  (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same
  code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not**
  change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change
  discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the
  scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public
  `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests;
  generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`
  (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`,
  run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`,
  `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in
  `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's
  store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired;
  hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via
  shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the
  weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not
  levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal
  `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers
  the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level
  readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe
every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add
integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and
run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and
assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the
GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene:
  round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a
  level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests
  (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart,
  every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling
  real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert
  `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the
  duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not
  duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD;
  otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to
  name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay
  or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record
  any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable
  under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle
  **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to
  `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an
  optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.
- **HUD coupling (assumption):** the shared HUD has no power-up level readout;
  keep the new readout gym-local to avoid changing shared HUD behaviour.
- **Parity-test flakiness (risk):** booting two Phaser games per case under
  parallel load is slow; reuse the existing generous timeout pattern and a
  single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots.
- **Reset-on-run-restart (ambiguity):** the gym must offer a deterministic way
  to exercise `resetPowerUpLevels` for the reset test; expose a public
  restart/reset hook (test-only seam) rather than relying on a real GameOver.
- **Determinism (constraint):** all tests drive `tick(dt)`, no wall-clock.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups (parent /
  `discovered-from`). Ships the model this gym demonstrates.
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wire power-up level curves into `EffectsRegistry`
  and the shared effect path (predecessor; makes field pickups level up).
- **AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB** — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb
  (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the
  hold-full choice.
- **AH-0MUWGD0EN008T3TY** — P4 model: `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` replace
  `bombCharges` (supersedes the original P4 axis).
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** — Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration
  tests (the direct structural precedent; mirrors the same shape for weapons).
- **AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA** — Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining
  core-code duplication (the parity convention this item must respect).
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** — Test: P10 parity across `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals`
  and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (precedent for real-gym parity tests).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD** – Documentation for combat spawning (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, assert, body (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, applies, assert, body, combatscene (+20 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, body, combatscene (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was conducted: the seed context plus the
shipped model, the wiring predecessors and the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
were sufficient to draft a clear brief (intake SKILL §4 — skip the interview
when seed context suffices; AGENTS.md — do not ask unnecessary questions). Each
apparent design choice is recorded below with the evidence that resolved it and
the documented assumption taken where evidence was partial.

- **Q (resolved from the work item + precedent): Should this be a new dedicated
  gym or an extension of `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymPowerUpsUtility`?**
  — Answer: a **new** `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene. Evidence: the work-item title
  and description say "Add a gym scene"; the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
  (AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J) established a dedicated leveling gym; `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers `Gym<Name>.ts`. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- **Q (resolved from the work item): What is the parity-test scope?**
  — Answer: boot the **real** gym and assert the shared power-up level path is
  identical to `PlayScene`, not another minimal `EquivGymScene`. Evidence: the
  description explicitly requires game↔gym parity "for the shared power-up level
  path" and names the duplicate-body guard. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): Should the gym include combat threats so P3/P4/P6/P7
  behaviour is fully observable?**
  — Answer (assumed, producer may override): threat-free readout gallery as the
  default, with an optional threat toggle only if the parity tests require
  observable combat behaviour. Evidence: `GymWeaponLeveling` is threat-free and
  demonstrates levels via a readout; `GymPowerUpsCombat` already owns the
  threat-based P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour. Source: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): What demonstrates "level" — a shared HUD readout or
  a gym-local panel?**
  — Answer (assumed): gym-local readout over `PowerUpLevelStore` /
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`; avoid changing shared HUD behaviour. Evidence: the
  shared HUD has only a weapon-level readout; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the
  established gym-local `.gym-panel` pattern. Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): How does the gym exercise level reset?**
  — Answer (assumed): expose a deterministic public restart/reset hook on the
  gym scene so the reset test does not depend on a real GameOver sequence.
  Source: `Player.getPowerUpLevels` / `resetPowerUpLevels`
  (`src/entities/Player.ts`).
- **Observation:** the automated `find-related` report surfaced only generic
  matches (enemy gym, difficulty curve, combat-spawning docs); the higher-signal
  relationships above were found by manual worklog search and file inspection.

# Scripted Gameplay Videos (Multi-Scene Capture)

In a scripted video capture we create a level, play it for x seconds, then capture y seconds, pause the video capture. Create a new level, play it for x seconds, capture y seconds. There should be a fade to black and a fade from black lasting 0.25 seconds between each scene. There are an arbitrary number of scenes.

## Problem statement

The current capture system produces a single continuous video — either one full demo run with tail, or a fixed-length scripted clip. This feature adds **multi-scene** capture: sequence several gameplay segments (levels or gyms), play each for a configured duration, capture each for a configured duration, and stitch them into one video with fade transitions (0.25 s black fade in/out) between scenes.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can define a sequence of scenes and capture each one with play/capture durations and fade transitions, producing a single compiled video showing multiple gameplay segments for demo / showcase / marketing purposes.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants to create showcase videos that demonstrate several distinct gameplay elements (different gyms, boss phases, power-up interactions) in one compiled video, rather than multiple separate recordings.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — single-scene capture orchestrator
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — scripted bot plan + probe helpers
- `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` — run-end signal, tail/cap logic
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — hermetic tests
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documentation
- `src/scenes/gym/` — individual gym scenes (each exercises one mechanic), discovered dynamically via `import.meta.glob`
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — dev gym index (reached from the menu's "Gym Scene Index (dev)" control)
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — URL-selected dev scenarios (`boss-four-hits`, `boss`, `defeat`) with a page-side release handle
- No fade/transition or multi-scene stitching exists in capture tooling.

## Desired change

1. A capture mode that defines a **scene list** (via a config file — see Q1) — each entry specifying the target, play duration (x), and capture duration (y).
2. Between each scene, a **fade-to-black (0.25 s)** then **fade-from-black (0.25 s)** transition is rendered **page-side** and captured by the running recorder.
3. The final output is a **single stitched WebM** containing all scenes with transitions, written to the configured output path.

## Design decisions (producer answers)

- **Q1 — Scene-list specification:** **A (config file).** A JSON config file lists the scenes with their targets and play/capture durations.
- **Q3 — Fade rendering:** **A (page-side canvas overlay).** The fade is drawn over the canvas by the capture (Playwright injection), so the continuously-running `MediaRecorder` captures it and no game-side change is needed. Because one recorder runs across all scenes, scene switching must happen **in-page** (a page reload would end the recorder).
- **Q2 — Scene target:** OPEN — expanded analysis posted in the comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6` (options A gym scene keys / B dev scenarios / C generated game levels / D generic scene key; recommended A). Pending producer choice.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — new flags/mode for scene lists
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (new) — scene-list config parsing, batch orchestration, page-side fade overlay, and single-output stitching
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — new tests for scene parsing, fade timing, and stitch logic
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documentation
- `src/` — a small dev-gated page-side scene-start hook, if Q2 resolves to A/B/C/D (exact location depends on the Q2 answer)

## Open Questions (need producer review)

**Q2: What does each scene target, and how is it started?** — full analysis in comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6`:

- **A.** Gym scene keys (e.g. `GymPlayer`, `GymScout`, `GymWeapons`, `GymBoss`) — widest showcase variety, least per-scene work; dev-only scenes. *(Recommended)*
- **B.** Dev scenarios (e.g. `boss-four-hits`, `defeat`) — real gameplay but verification-oriented; each new variant is a `src/` change.
- **C.** Generated game levels (shipped `PlayScene`, fresh level per scene) — literal match to the brief; multi-wave, needs a dev hook.
- **D.** Arbitrary registered scene key — maximally flexible; best as the internal mechanism, not a separate feature.

## Appendix: Interview Q&A

- **Q1 (Map, to producer): Scene list specification?** — **ANSWERED:** **A** — JSON config file. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (Map, to producer): Scene target specification?** — **EXPANDED, OPEN.** Options and impacts posted in comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6` after producer asked for more detail. Recommended: A (gym scene keys).
- **Q3 (Map, to producer): Fade rendering method?** — **ANSWERED:** **A** — page-side canvas overlay via Playwright. Source: interactive reply.

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

- A short design note is recorded on this item comparing (a) the level-based temporary model chosen in AH-0MUX802450085VZZ vs (b) a distinct consumable-grant type.
- Recommendation (with rationale) is recorded and the producing work item is linked.
- If a change is recommended, follow-up implementation work items are created; otherwise the item is closed as 'no change required'.

## Notes
- This item is NOT blocking AH-0MUX802450085VZZ, which proceeds with decision (b): unconsumed grants persist until consumed and are not removed on expiry.

# Epic: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Problem

The shipped attract/demo bot (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ and its follow-ups) is a
per-frame priority ladder with a reaction-time governor bolted on. It has no
commitment, no forward model, no aim/fire reasoning and no way to learn from
human play, so it reads as random and cannot be tuned into competence. We need
a **maintainable bot framework** that plays competently and human-like, adapts
to new content (enemies, power-ups, weapons) without a rewrite, can be re-run
headless for reproducible evaluation, and is backed by **telemetry** gathered
both from our own recordings and from production playtesters.

## Goals / user stories

- **As the maintainer**, I can re-run the bot headless on a fixed seed and get
  reproducible results, so I can improve it safely.
- **As the maintainer**, I can add a new enemy / power-up / weapon and have the
  bot handle it through configuration, without touching the core.
- **As the maintainer**, I can record human play and analyse it (reaction
  times, target choices, engagement distances, dodge behaviour) to tune and
  evaluate the bot.
- **As the maintainer**, I can enable opt-in telemetry in production and gather
  playtester data (state + input + events) to improve the bot and the game.
- **As a player**, I see an attract/demo mode that looks like a competent
  player.

## Design overview

- **Determinism.** A per-run **seed** drives all gameplay RNG (wave/spawn/
  timing) so a run is reproducible and the bot can be evaluated same-seed.
- **Telemetry.** A **versioned, consent-gated, pluggable** pipeline. Records
  are per-tick state + input + discrete events, tagged with the run seed and a
  schema version. Sinks: a local JSONL dev sink and a production remote sink.
  No PII; **disabled by default in production**, opt-in only.
- **Bot framework.** A world model (from `BotSnapshot`), a **registry of
  goals/behaviours**, a **utility selector with commitment/hysteresis**, a
  behaviour-tree executor, and predictive **dodge/aim** behaviours.
  Content-specific parameters live in a **config/registry** so new content is
  data, not code.
- **Evaluation.** Same-seed bot-vs-human runs, metrics, A/B comparisons and
  side-by-side clips.
- **Style matching (later).** Fit parameters or train a policy from recorded
  telemetry once the competent bot exists.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** Runs are reproducible from a seed; the seed is recorded in
  telemetry; a headless runner executes the bot for N ticks on a seed and
  produces a deterministic report.
- **AC2:** Telemetry is a pluggable framework with a documented, versioned
  schema, disabled by default in production and opt-in consent-gated; it
  records per-tick state + input + events with the seed and is a no-op when
  disabled.
- **AC3:** The bot is a structured framework (world model + goal/behaviour
  registry + committed selection + predictive dodge/aim), not a per-frame
  priority ladder; new enemies/power-ups/weapons are handled via config with
  tests.
- **AC4:** The competent bot completes representative runs with human-like
  behaviour (goal commitment, no suicide, human cadence) and passes an
  evaluation report (survival, minerals/min, targets engaged, dodges).
- **AC5:** Human play can be recorded and analysed offline, and a replay/ghost
  viewer compares bot vs human on the same seed.
- **AC6:** Production telemetry can be enabled by a playtester via an explicit
  opt-in, with privacy documentation and no PII.
- **AC7:** All documentation is updated (framework, extension guide, telemetry
  schema/privacy); full suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Out of scope (this epic)

- A fully style-matched clone of a specific player (style matching is an
  early-phase deliverable; full fidelity is a later follow-up).
- Server-side ML training infrastructure or online multiplayer.
- CI wiring of the capture/eval jobs (follow-up once the harness exists).

## Children (dependency order)

1. Deterministic run seeding + seed plumbing.
2. Telemetry framework (versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag).
3. Game telemetry instrumentation (per-tick state + events).
4. Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling.
5. Bot framework core (world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy,
   content config).
6. Structured competent bot (utility goals + behaviour tree + predictive
   dodge/aim).
7. Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons.
8. Same-seed evaluation harness (metrics, A/B, side-by-side clips).
9. Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation).
10. Production telemetry (opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink, docs).

## Related work

Builds on AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ (Smart capture bot) and its follow-ups
AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB (human-like input) and AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L (movement
goals). Supersedes the per-frame priority-ladder design.

# Flaky PlayScene AC4 victory-celebration SHUTDOWN test under heavy load

**Headline:** Two `PlayScene` victory/transition tests wait on a wall-clock
`setTimeout(VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500)` and race Phaser's delayed
`GameOverScene` transition under heavy machine load; make them advance the
Phaser clock deterministically so the full suite is trustworthy again.

## Problem statement

`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` contains two tests that assert the run has
transitioned to `GameOverScene` (or that the victory celebration has been
torn down) by sleeping a real `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500` ms and then
asserting on live scene state. The production transition is a Phaser
`this.time.delayedCall(VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS, …)`; under CPU/timer
contention the wall-clock sleep can expire before the scene clock has
advanced far enough, so the assertion observes the pre-transition state.

- Reported failure (2026-10-07, full suite under heavy multi-agent load):
  `Tests 1 failed | 3509 passed` at the AC4 SHUTDOWN assertion
  (`expect(effect.active).toBe(false)`), then **passed on immediate re-run**
  (`152 files / 3510 tests passed`).
- The flake is test-harness nondeterminism, not a production defect: the
  live requestAnimationFrame loop advances the scene by an amount that depends
  on machine load, so a fixed real-time wait is not a reliable barrier.

## Users

- **Test maintainers / release engineers:** need a green full suite so a
  random failure does not mask a real regression or block `dev` → `main`.
- **Developers:** need to add/extend victory and teardown tests without
  inheriting a load-sensitive sleep.

**Example user stories**

- As a developer, I want the victory-transition tests to be deterministic
  under load, so a full-suite run is a trustworthy signal.
- As a release engineer, I want flaky PlayScene tests eliminated, so the
  release pipeline is not blocked by a phantom failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deterministic clock:** Neither affected test depends on a
  wall-clock `setTimeout` that can be missed under load. Each advances the
  Phaser clock deterministically (stop the live loop and pump the scene clock,
  e.g. `game.loop.stop()` + `game.step(simTime, STEP_MS)` / a `stepUntil`
  predicate) **or** waits on the scene/transition state rather than elapsed
  real time.
- **AC2 — Repeatable under load:** The affected tests pass deterministically
  when the full suite is run **3 consecutive times** on a loaded machine (or
  with elevated `--maxConcurrency`), with zero failures attributable to these
  tests.
- **AC3 — No regressions:** No other PlayScene (or other suite) tests regress,
  and production behaviour — the `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS` victory hold and
  the `SHUTDOWN` teardown of the celebration — is unchanged.
- **AC4 — Test/validation coverage:** The fix includes a meaningful
  testing/validation criterion that exercises the deterministic path (i.e. the
  test itself proves the transition/teardown without relying on elapsed wall
  time), and the pattern is documented where a future author can reuse it.
- **AC5 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site
  entries. (CHANGELOG.md is out of scope — owned by the ship release pipeline.)
- **AC6 — Full suite:** Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-harness only:** do not change production `PlayScene` victory/teardown
  behaviour; only the test harness (and, at most, a clarifying production
  comment) may change. Preserve `deterministicBoot: true`.
- **No meaningful slowdown:** the deterministic stepping must not materially
  increase suite runtime.
- **Reuse existing patterns:** mirror the established `game.step` +
  `stepUntil` approach already used in `PlaySceneSeeding.test.ts` and
  `PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts` rather than inventing a new mechanism.
- **Gym↔game parity:** not applicable — this is a test harness change with no
  gameplay behaviour change (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1).
- **UK English** in all comments and documentation.
- **Isolation:** keep the change scoped to the failure; do not fold in
  unrelated test refactors.

## Existing state

- `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS = ENDOFRUN_VICTORY_FIREWORKS_DURATION_MS`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` ≈ line 240).
- `_finishRunWithPurpose(won)` schedules the transition via
  `this.time.delayedCall(VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS, () => this._finishRun(won))`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` ≈ line 1690). Its doc comment already notes that a
  zero hold transitions immediately to keep timing tests deterministic.
- **Two** tests use the wall-clock pattern `await new Promise((r) =>
  setTimeout(r, VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500))`:
  1. `PlayScene — boss encounter` → **"AC4 — defeating all 4 phases wins the
     run at the game-over screen"** (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` ≈ line 1613).
  2. `PlayScene — end-of-run victory trigger` → **"AC4 — the victory
     celebration is destroyed on SHUTDOWN (no leaks)"**
     (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` ≈ line 3923) — the reported failure.
- Established deterministic stepping already exists:
  `booted.game.loop.stop()` + `game.step(simTime, STEP_MS)` and a `stepUntil`
  predicate (`src/scenes/PlaySceneSeeding.test.ts` ≈ lines 55–70;
  `src/scenes/PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts` ≈ lines 80–90).
- Precedent: `reachBoss()` was previously made load-robust by polling the
  `WaveManager` flags instead of `getBoss()` (AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM).

## Desired change

Replace both wall-clock waits with deterministic Phaser-clock advancement
(stop the live loop and step a fixed simulated time past
`VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS`, or poll a scene/transition predicate with a hard
failure message), so the tests assert the same behaviour without depending on
real elapsed time. Keep assertions and coverage identical; document the
deterministic pattern at the point of use.

## Validation approach

- Target only the affected tests while iterating:
  `npx vitest run src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts -t "AC4"`
- Prove repeatability under load (AC2): run the full suite three times with
  elevated concurrency:
  `for i in 1 2 3; do npm test -- --maxConcurrency 50 || exit 1; done`
- Confirm production behaviour is untouched: `git diff src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
  shows comment-only changes (or nothing).
- Final gate: run the full suite via `/skill:test` before `in_review`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — replace the two
  `setTimeout(VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500)` waits (≈ lines 1613 and
  3923) with deterministic clock advancement / state polling; possibly add a
  small shared `stepPastVictoryHold` helper.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — reference only; `_finishRunWithPurpose` (≈ line
  1690) documents the hold. Production logic unchanged.
- `src/scenes/PlaySceneSeeding.test.ts` / `src/scenes/PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts`
  — existing `game.step` + `stepUntil` patterns to mirror (reference only).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption A1 (scope):** Both wall-clock waits share the same root cause,
  so both are fixed in this work item; fixing only the reported AC4 SHUTDOWN
  test would leave an identical load-sensitive flake behind. Recorded for
  producer confirmation.
- **Assumption A2:** The flake is harness nondeterminism, not a production
  race — supported by the pass-on-rerun evidence and the existing zero-hold
  deterministic hook. If stepping the clock exposes a genuine ordering bug,
  raise a separate work item rather than widening this one.
- **Risk R1 — clock semantics:** Phaser's `Clock` advances through
  `game.step`; a naive `scene.tick()` loop may not advance `delayedCall`. The
  fix must verify which driver advances the timer.
- **Risk R2 — stepping budget:** An unbounded step loop could hide a stalled
  transition; use a bounded `stepUntil` predicate that fails loudly.
- **Risk R3 — scope creep:** Additional flaky waits discovered elsewhere
  should become linked work items (`discovered-from:`), not be folded in.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUZMTU3Y001Y8XZ** – Verify gym-game parity and full test suite (blocked)
- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** – Flaky tests: PlayScene and GymFormationScene fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load (completed)
- **AH-0MUWTNPY8003GGAA** – capture: add progress/ETA output and dependency preflight (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance, active (+69 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, active, agent (+64 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, active (+59 more)

**Manual cross-references**

- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** — closest precedent: deterministic makeover of
  `PlayScene` boss tests (`reachBoss` flag polling) after full-suite parallel
  flakiness; the same load-sensitivity root cause.
- **AH-0MUXZ4D0M001IWW1** — `discovered-from` parent (full-run capture
  integration verification); this item was discovered during that run.
- **AH-0MUZMTU3Y001Y8XZ** — "Verify gym-game parity and full test suite"
  (blocked): consumes a trustworthy full suite; a green suite here unblocks the
  evidence that item needs.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Clarifying questions:** none required — the seed context (problem,
  reproduction, expected behaviour and a concrete implementation sketch)
  was sufficient to draft this brief without an interview round.
- **Assumption A1 (recorded, not a question):** both wall-clock waits are
  treated as in scope; see Risks and assumptions above.
- **Assumption A2 (recorded, not a question):** harness-only fix; production
  behaviour unchanged.

# Intake Brief: Add --count/-n option to gameplay capture

## Problem statement

`npm run capture` records exactly one clip per invocation. Collecting N clips requires a shell loop that repeatedly boots the Vite dev server, re-warms the game, and re-installs Playwright bookkeeping — making batch capture unnecessarily slow.

## Users

- **Maintainer/Producer:** needs to collect batches of gameplay clips (e.g. 50 runs) for regression testing, review, or analysis without paying the boot cost per iteration.
- **CI/automation:** wants efficient batch capture without fragile shell loops.

## User stories

- As a maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --count 3` (or `-n 3`) to produce 3 distinct `.webm` files in a single process, so I don't need a slow shell loop.
- As a maintainer, I want each iteration to reuse a single Vite dev server and browser session, so batch capture is fast.
- As a maintainer, I want `--output` + `--count` to produce deterministically named files (or fail clearly), so I can predict output locations.
- As a maintainer, I want `--json` to report per-iteration results, so automation can parse outcomes.
- As a maintainer, I want a failed iteration to not silently hide its failure, so I can debug and fix issues.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `npm run capture -- --count 3` produces 3 distinct non-trivial `.webm` files in `capture-output/` and exits 0.
2. `-n` is accepted as a short alias for `--count`.
3. Omitting `--count` behaves exactly as today (single clip, no regression).
4. `--count` with a non-positive / non-numeric value fails fast with a clear message and non-zero exit code.
5. Multi-iteration runs reuse a single dev server (no repeated boot per iteration) — verified by log/probe evidence or a test.
6. `--output` + `--count > 1` behaviour is deterministic, documented and covered by a test.
7. `--json` output reports per-iteration results including file paths.
8. `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents `--count`/`-n` and the output-naming rules.
9. Unit tests cover arg parsing (default, valid, invalid, alias) and the multi-output path resolver.

## Constraints

- Preserve existing single-clip behaviour as the default (count=1).
- `--scripted`, `--scenario`, `--tail`, `--max-duration`, `--warmup` apply to every iteration.
- The Vite dev server and browser session must be kept alive between iterations where safe.
- A failure in one iteration must be attributable: summary names the failing iteration, exit code is non-zero.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` records exactly one clip per invocation.
- Output defaults to `capture-output/gameplay-<ISO-timestamp>.webm` (ms precision) or an explicit `--output`.
- No `--count`/`-n` flag exists.
- Workaround is a shell loop: `for i in {1..50}; do npm run capture || break; done`.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — Extend `parseCaptureArgs` with `--count`/`-n`, add iteration loop
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — Unit tests for arg parsing and multi-output naming
- `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` — Shared lifecycle helpers used by capture
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — Update documentation with new flags
- `package.json` — No changes needed (script already exists)

## Related work

- **Batch scenario listing and multi-video capture** (AH-0MUZM8ATZ002AKFP) — `related-to`; the broader batch capture feature that also includes `--count N` (AC3). This item is a subset.
- **Capture tooling records the in-game demo** (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V) — `related-to`; the original capture feature.
- **Document full-run capture and dwell** (AH-0MUXZ4DDV0098ZW4) — `related-to`; documentation context.

## Risks, assumptions and failure modes

- **Assumption:** keeping the Vite server and browser alive across iterations is safe. Mitigation: use fresh page/context per iteration (same approach as batch capture in the broader item).
- **Risk:** timestamp collisions in tight loops. Mitigation: include iteration index in default output names to guarantee uniqueness.
- **Risk:** `--output` + `--count > 1` collision. Mitigation: either reject the combination with a clear error, or infer an indexed suffix (recommended: reject with a clear error, as this is simpler and safer).
- **Risk:** a per-item failure may leave the browser/server in an unknown state. Mitigation: per-item error recovery and continue to next iteration, or abort — producer decision needed.
- **Scope-creep risk:** adding `--scenario` support per-iteration, or parallel capture, or video joining is out of scope. Record as `discovered-from` work items.

## Open question for producer

- **Output naming when `--output` is supplied with `--count > 1`:** reject the combination with a clear error, or infer indexed suffixes (e.g. `demo-1.webm`, `demo-2.webm`)? *Recommended: reject with a clear error — simpler, avoids surprising file names.*
- **Failure handling across iterations:** if one iteration fails, continue to remaining iterations or abort? *Recommended: continue, so partial results are still captured.*

## Appendix: clarification

- No interactive interview was required. The work item was already sufficiently defined with a problem statement, user stories, 9 measurable ACs, constraints, key files, and related work.
- Q (intake evaluation, this session, Map): "Is an interactive interview necessary?" — Answer (agent, Map): "No. The work item description already includes a clear goal, user story, 9 measurable acceptance criteria, constraints, suggested implementation, and related work. An interview would only repeat information already documented." Source: `wl show AH-0MUYTK941005E2M4 --json`.
- Overlap noted: the broader batch capture feature (AH-0MUZM8ATZ002AKFP) already includes `--count N` as AC3. This item's scope is a subset. Producer decision needed on relationship.

# Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

The stored **Teleport** power-up currently requires a manual **S / ↓** key press, overloading the movement keys and blocking the reverse thruster (AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG). Phase Shift is already reactive — it auto-triggers through the shared danger feed. We want Teleport to become **automatic** in the same way, so S / ↓ are freed for held reverse thrust and a stored Teleport is spent exactly when the ship is genuinely threatened.

## Users

- **Player** (primary): when a hostile threat closes in and I hold a stored Teleport, I want the teleport to fire automatically (like Phase Shift) so I am not required to reach for a key mid-dodge, and so movement keys are never overloaded with a consumable ability.
- **Player using the reverse thruster** (dependent work item AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG): I need S / ↓ to be reliably mine for held reverse thrust, with no Teleport consumption firing on the same keys.
- **Developer / designer**: I need one shared, testable auto-trigger model so the game and every gym behave identically and cannot diverge.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when three or more hostile bodies/bullets close within 40 px and I hold a Teleport, the ship teleports automatically to the nearest safe spot along my heading and gains a brief Phase Shift on arrival — without any key press.
- As a player holding both a Phase Shift charge and a Teleport stack, the ability with more remaining charges is spent, keeping my scarcer resource for later.
- As a player who dislikes the automatic behaviour, I can rely on the documented re-arm rules (one activation per danger episode) rather than having teleports drained continuously.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Auto-trigger on the shared danger feed.** Teleport auto-activates with **no key press** when the ship is in danger — the existing shared `isInDanger` definition (combined hostile bodies + enemy bullets within `DANGER_RADIUS` = 40 px is `>= DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD` = 3) — the danger has cleared since the last defensive activation, and the re-arm cooldown has elapsed. No new danger definition, radius or threshold is introduced; the game and every gym feed the same signal.
2. **AC2 — Charge-count selection between Phase Shift and Teleport.** At each activation opportunity the resolver chooses which defence to spend by comparing the **available counts**: Phase Shift auto-activation charges (`phaseCharges()`) versus stored Teleport stacks (`teleportStacks()`).
   - If only one ability is available, it is used.
   - If both are available, the ability with the **greater count** is used (spending the more abundant stock first).
   - On a **tie**, the choice is a uniform **50/50 random** pick.
   - If neither is available, nothing fires.
   - A **permanent Phase Shift** (unlimited activations) is treated as an **unbounded** count and therefore always wins the comparison — stored Teleports are conserved while permanent Phase Shift is owned (documented assumption, revisitable).
   - The RNG is **injectable/seeded** so the tie-break is deterministically testable.
3. **AC3 — Teleport activation semantics are unchanged.** When Teleport is chosen it uses the existing `CombatScene.triggerTeleport` path: nearest safe spot along the heading (screen-clamped, existing enemy/bullet avoidance radii), consumes **exactly one FIFO stack**, grants the existing Phase Shift on arrival, and plays the existing Phase Shift activation cue. Stacking/level-store consumption semantics are untouched.
4. **AC4 — No manual S / ↓ activation of Teleport remains.** `CombatScene._handleTeleport`, the `teleportKey`/`downKey` fields, the hard-coded ↓ fallback and every `_handleTeleport()` call site (`PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymFormationScene`) are removed; nothing consumes S / ↓ for Teleport any more. The `layerDrop` rebindable action is no longer wired to Teleport; per the producer, its action definition is **retained (unwired)** so the dependent reverse-thruster item AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG can reuse/repurpose or remove it (coordination recorded on that item).
5. **AC5 — Re-arm / cooldown matches the Phase Shift model.** A single shared re-arm governor enforces **at most one defensive activation per danger episode**: after activation, no further auto-trigger until the danger has dropped below the threshold **and** a re-arm cooldown (mirroring `PHASE_REARM_COOLDOWN` = 0.5 s) has elapsed, so a permanent Phase Shift remains powerful but never perpetual and Teleports are not drained in one continuous threat.
6. **AC6 — Gym↔game parity (one implementation).** The selection, re-arm and danger feed live once in the shared combat core (`CombatScene` + `EffectsRegistry`) and run from the single existing per-frame danger-dispatch call site in `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat`; no scene re-implements it and the duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and gym-parity docs assertion pass. The Teleport side still honours `canTeleport()` (the gym opt-in gate) and the FPS-order (danger fed immediately before collision gating) so an activation this frame protects this frame.
7. **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD controls table — S / ↓ no longer Teleport, now reserved for reverse thrust; §4.4 Teleport row and note; §6.4 gym descriptions that reference S / ↓ teleport; the Phase Shift activation-sound note; the project-structure/controls summary; code comments), including the auto-trigger selection rule and the removal of S / ↓ for Teleport.
8. **AC8 — Tests.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes, with new/updated tests covering: auto-trigger on danger; no trigger when danger is below threshold; count-comparison selection (Teleport > Phase Shift → Teleport; Phase Shift > Teleport → Phase Shift); tie-break via a seeded RNG reaching each outcome; permanent Phase Shift outranking Teleport; re-arm blocked while continuously in danger and while the cooldown is running; FIFO consume-exactly-once; no manual key path remains; and gym↔game parity. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline. CI/CD pipeline tests are excluded.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity.** One shared implementation in `src/scenes/core/` + `src/powerups/effects.ts`; no divergent copies; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard must pass.
- **Reuse the existing danger contract.** `isInDanger` / `countThreatsInRange` / `DANGER_RADIUS` / `DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD` are used as-is; do not fork the threshold.
- **Preserve Teleport's warp semantics** (`findTeleportDestination`, safe-spot resolution, screen clamp, FIFO consumption, Phase Shift-on-arrival) and the level-store charge model.
- **Preserve `canTeleport()`** as the gym opt-in gate for auto-triggers.
- **Deterministic tests:** the tie-break RNG must be injectable/seeded; no reliance on global `Math.random()`.
- **Backward compatibility:** hold-full Teleport rewards and the HUD teleport stack readout keep working; no persisted-data change is expected.
- Applies to every combat scene; non-combat gyms (no hostile threats) never reach the danger threshold, so behaviour there is unchanged.

## Existing state

- **Phase Shift is already automatic.** `CombatScene._updatePhaseShiftAutoTrigger(dt)` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) builds the hostile body/bullet lists, calls the pure `isInDanger(player, bodies, bullets)` helper (`src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts`), and feeds the result to `EffectsRegistry.updateDanger(inDanger, dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`). The registry owns charge availability, the danger-cleared re-arm flag and the `PHASE_REARM_COOLDOWN`; it activates Phase Shift for the level-resolved duration, consumes one charge (permanent never consumes) and returns whether it fired; the scene plays `playPhaseShiftSound()` on fire. Every combat scene calls it once per frame immediately before `_handleCollisions`.
- **Teleport is manual.** `CombatScene._handleTeleport()` (JustDown semantics) reads `teleportKey` (the `layerDrop` binding) and a hard-coded `downKey` (↓) fallback, then calls `triggerTeleport()`. `triggerTeleport()` checks `canTeleport()`, `registry.hasTeleport()`, resolves the destination via `findTeleportDestination`, consumes one stack via `registry.consumeTeleport()` (which also grants Phase Shift), and repositions the player. Call sites: `PlayScene.tick`, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`, `GymFormationScene` tick.
- **Bindings.** `layerDrop` (default `'s'`, intentionally overlapping `moveDown`) is defined in `src/core/settingsStore.ts`, shown in `SettingsScene.ts` as "Layer Drop", and used only to wire `teleportKey` in `PlayScene`. The reverse-thruster item AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG depends on this item and will own S / ↓ (`moveDown`).
- **Level model.** Phase Shift charges and Teleport stacks are both level-derived from the single run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` owned by `Player`; `phaseCharges()` is `0` for a permanent reward and `teleportStacks()` is the stored FIFO count. Teleport has no "permanent" variant.

## Desired change

- Add a shared **auto-defence selector** to the combat core / effects registry that runs from the per-frame danger feed and decides, per danger episode, between Phase Shift and Teleport using the producer's charge-count rule (AC2), with an injectable RNG for the tie-break.
- Extend the per-frame danger dispatch so that: when `isInDanger` is true, the re-arm governor allows an activation, and the selected defence is **Teleport**, the scene performs `triggerTeleport()` (which consumes one FIFO stack and grants Phase Shift on arrival); when the selected defence is **Phase Shift**, the existing registry activation path runs unchanged.
- Keep **one shared re-arm governor** so at most one defensive activation happens per danger episode (danger-cleared + cooldown), regardless of which ability fired.
- Remove the manual Teleport path: `_handleTeleport`, `teleportKey`, `downKey`, the ↓ fallback and all call sites. Leave the `layerDrop` action defined but unwired (coordination with AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG).

## Problem

Running `npm run build` from a git worktree created by the implement skill fails at the `build-audio` step:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'tsx' imported from /home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules/toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js
```

## Root cause

`scripts/build-audio.mjs` `resolveToneForge()` resolves the sibling checkout as `join(repoRoot, '..', 'ToneForge')`. Inside a worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`) that path is `.worklog/worktrees/ToneForge`, which does not exist, so resolution falls through to `tf` on PATH (`node_modules/.bin/tf -> ../toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js`). That copy has no `tsx` dependency, so the CLI crashes.

When built from the main checkout the sibling path resolves correctly and the build succeeds.

## Workaround used

`TONEFORGE_CLI=/home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js npm run build` (the sibling's `node_modules` has `tsx`).

## Expected behaviour

`npm run build` succeeds inside a worktree without requiring `TONEFORGE_CLI` to be set manually, since worktrees are the mandated implementation workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `npm run build` succeeds from a worktree with no `TONEFORGE_CLI` set.
- AC2: Sibling resolution is anchored to the main checkout (e.g. via the git common dir) rather than the worktree root.
- AC3: Existing `build-audio` tests still pass and the main-checkout build is unaffected.

# Batch scenario / multi-video capture tooling

## Problem statement

`npm run capture` produces exactly one video per invocation, and `--scenario`
accepts a single, unlisted value. There is no way to (a) discover which dev
scenarios exist, (b) run every scenario in one call, or (c) generate N videos
without a shell loop that pays the Vite + Chromium startup cost on every run.

**User stories:**

- As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` to show every
  implemented dev scenario (name + one-line effect) so I do not have to read the
  source.
- As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --all-scenarios` to produce one
  video per scenario in a single command, reusing one Vite server and one
  browser session.
- As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --count N` (optionally with
  `--scenario`) to produce N videos as review / regression evidence.
- As a producer/reviewer, I want a final batch summary and a non-zero exit when
  any item fails, so a batch can gate CI.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `parseCaptureArgs`: a single `scenario`
  string; flags are `--duration`, `--tail`, `--max-duration`, `--warmup`,
  `--output`, `--port`, `--headed`, `--json`, `--keep-server`, `--scripted`,
  `--scenario`.
- `runCapture` boots one Vite dev server + one Chromium browser per invocation
  and writes one output WebM.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` is the game-side resolver: `boss`, `boss-four-hits`,
  `defeat` (plus the default no-scenario demo run). The Node capture tool does
  not import it; `--scenario` is passed through the URL unvalidated (an unknown
  value silently runs the normal demo).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents the three scenario values in a table.
- There is no `--list-scenarios`, `--all-scenarios` or `--count`, and no shared
  scenario registry between the game and the Node tool.

## Desired change

1. **Scenario registry (single source).** Add a shared, pure scenario registry
   (name + short description) usable by both the game resolver and the Node
   capture tool, so the list cannot drift. Likely a browser-free `.mjs` module
   (mirroring `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`) that `src/core/devScenario.ts`
   consumes.
2. **`--list-scenarios`.** Print the implemented scenarios in human-readable
   form, or machine-readable JSON with `--json`; exit 0 without booting
   Vite/Chromium.
3. **`--all-scenarios`.** Run every registered scenario in one invocation, one
   video each, continuing past a per-item failure and reporting a per-item plus
   aggregate result.
4. **`--count N`.** Produce N videos (the default demo run, or N of a given
   `--scenario`).
5. **Single-session batch.** Reuse one Vite server and one Chromium browser
   across the batch, with a fresh page/context per item so a failed clip cannot
   poison the next.
6. **Output naming.** Deterministic, collision-free default names per item;
   document how `--output` behaves for batches (directory or prefix).
7. **Summary + exit code.** Final summary (path, outcome, complete/capHit,
   bytes per item); exit non-zero if any item failed or hit the cap.
8. **Backwards compatibility.** A single `--scenario` invocation behaves exactly
   as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (list):** `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` lists every implemented
  scenario (value + one-line effect) from the shared registry, exits 0, and
  boots no browser or server; `--json` emits a machine-readable array.
- **AC2 (all):** `npm run capture -- --all-scenarios` produces one video per
  registered scenario in a single invocation and reports success/failure per
  item.
- **AC3 (count):** `npm run capture -- --count N` produces exactly N videos
  (N >= 1); with `--scenario S` all N use S, otherwise the default demo run;
  `--count 0`, missing or non-numeric values error clearly.
- **AC4 (single session):** across a batch the Vite server and Chromium browser
  start exactly once (asserted via instrumentation/count), with a fresh
  page/context per item.
- **AC5 (naming):** items get deterministic, collision-free default output
  paths; an existing file is never silently overwritten by a different item.
- **AC6 (summary/exit):** a batch prints a final aggregate summary and exits
  non-zero if any item failed or hit the cap; a single-item failure does not
  abort the remaining items.
- **AC7 (tests):** hermetic unit tests cover arg parsing (`--list-scenarios`,
  `--all-scenarios`, `--count`, combinations and invalid input), the registry
  contents, output-name generation, and batch result/exit-code aggregation
  (no browser); existing capture tests continue to pass.
- **AC8 (docs):** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the `README.md` capture
  section document the list/all/count flags with examples; `--help` updated.
- **AC9 (suite):** `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Constraints

- Capture stays outside the shipped bundle; the shared registry must be
  browser-free and consumed by dev-gated code only.
- The browser/encode path cannot run under vitest (the canvas is stubbed), so
  all new decision logic (registry, naming, aggregation) must be pure and
  unit-tested; the browser path is exercised by `npm run capture`.
- Serial-by-default batched execution (one browser) to avoid host resource
  contention.
- Existing single-scenario, `--duration` and `--scripted` behaviour unchanged.

## Risks, assumptions and failure modes

- **Assumption:** the three registered scenarios (`boss`, `boss-four-hits`,
  `defeat`) stay the complete set. Because the registry becomes the single
  source, a future scenario added in `src/core/devScenario.ts` without
  registering it would drift from the CLI. Mitigation: make the game resolver
  consume the registry and add a registry <-> resolver test.
- **Failure mode:** a per-item browser/encode failure must not poison the
  shared session (one Vite server + one Chromium browser). Mitigation: a fresh
  page/context per item, per-item error capture, and continue to the next item
  (AC6).
- **Failure mode:** deterministic default batch names could collide on a
  re-run, or an existing file could be silently overwritten by a different
  item. Mitigation: item-scoped, collision-free names plus a never-silently-
  overwrite check (AC5).
- **Failure mode:** a batch item that never signals a run-end could hang.
  Mitigation: the existing per-item `--max-duration` cap bounds each item and
  the summary reports `capHit` per item (AC6).
- **Risk (host resources):** parallel capture would exhaust CPU/GPU on the dev
  host, so execution stays serial by default (one browser; see Constraints).
- **Assumption:** `--list-scenarios` must not boot Vite/Chromium, so the
  registry has to be importable by bare Node — a browser-free `.mjs` module
  following the `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` precedent.
- **Scope-creep risk:** ad-hoc extras (a `--filter` flag, per-scenario duration
  overrides, an HTML index page) are out of scope; record each as a
  `discovered-from` work item rather than widening this change.

## OPEN QUESTIONs (non-blocking, recommended defaults)

- Should `--all-scenarios` include the default no-scenario demo run?
  *Recommended:* NO (an explicit `--include-demo` opt-in), because the demo is
  non-deterministic and multi-minute.
- `--output` in a batch: treat it as a directory (*recommended*) or a filename
  prefix?
- Should `--count` combine with `--all-scenarios` (N repeats of every scenario)?
  *Recommended:* reject the combination, or define it explicitly as N x all.
  Directed to the producer at plan/implement time.

## Key files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — flags, batch orchestration, summary/exit
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.d.mts` — types for new exports
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`) — shared browser-free scenario
  registry (or extend `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`)
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — consume the shared registry
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — hermetic tests
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `README.md` — documentation

## Related work

- **Create full video playthroughs** (AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU) — `discovered-from`;
  added the full-run capture and the `defeat` scenario this builds on.
- **Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic ...** (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) —
  `related-to`; the capture epic.
- **Spike: automated gameplay video capture** (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) — the
  pipeline this extends.

## Appendix: clarification

- The operator asked (this session) whether scenarios can be listed, all
  generated in one call, and N videos generated; none of the three exists today.
  This work item adds them. Approval to write code has NOT been given
  (create-only).
- Q (intake evaluation, this session, Map): "Is the work item defined well
  enough to skip the interactive interview?" — Answer (agent, Map): "Yes. The
  brief already carries a problem statement, user stories, 9 measurable ACs,
  constraints, key files and related work; an interactive interview would only
  repeat information already recorded in the work item." Source: `wl show
  AH-0MUZM8ATZ002AKFP --json`; repo inspection of
  `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`,
  `src/core/devScenario.ts`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `README.md`.
- OPEN QUESTION (retained for plan/implement; non-blocking, no answer supplied
  this session): demo inclusion in `--all-scenarios` (preferred **NO**;
  `--include-demo` opt-in), `--output` batch semantics (preferred a
  **directory**), and `--count` combined with `--all-scenarios` (preferred
  **reject**, or define as N x all). The recommended defaults are advisory; the
  producer's choice at plan time wins.
- Related-work research (find-related, this session): appended the automated
  report below (`AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN`, `AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123`,
  `AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C` plus three repo file matches); the manual **Related

# Report script counts soft-deleted children

**discovered-from:AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2**

## Problem

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) shows an incorrect **Children** count when a parent has soft-deleted children.

- `wl delete <id>` is a **soft delete** — it sets `status=deleted` and `deletedBy`, and the item remains visible via `wl show <parent> --children`.
- `wl list --parent <id>` correctly **excludes** deleted items.
- `render_report.py` (`render_from_wl`) counts `len(data["children"])` from `wl show --children`, so it **includes** the tombstones.

Observed on AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2: 7 active children + 6 soft-deleted coverage-gap children reported as `Children: 13`; `wl list --parent` correctly reports 7.

## Expected behaviour

The report's child count matches the active child set — i.e. it excludes items with `status=deleted` (or `deletedBy` set). Ideally the shared `wl show --children` behaviour and the report agree with `wl list --parent`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a parent with children.
2. `wl delete <one-child> --json` (soft delete).
3. Run `python3 skill/report/scripts/render_report.py <parent-id> --skill-name plan ...`.
4. Observe the **Children** count includes the deleted child.

## Suggested fix

Filter deleted children in `render_from_wl` before counting (e.g. `[c for c in children if c.get("status") != "deleted" and not c.get("deletedBy")]`), or make `wl show --children` exclude deleted items consistently with `wl list --parent`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The report's **Children** count excludes soft-deleted items.
- A test covers a parent with a mix of active and soft-deleted children.
- Behaviour is consistent with `wl list --parent`.

# Intake Brief — Explosions timed with the beat (AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3)

**Headline:** Player auto-fire already lands on a silent 80 BPM beat grid, but
non-weapon explosion SFX still fire on the exact death frame; schedule the
enemy/Diver/player destruction cues onto the next 16th note of the current
tempo so kills land rhythmically, while weapon cues keep their own
beat-synchronised firing pattern.

## Problem statement

`src/utils/beat.ts` already quantises every player weapon's fire to a silent,
configurable 80 BPM grid (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B), so shots are rhythmically
regular. The explosion sounds for a destroyed enemy, Diver or the player are
still dispatched immediately from the kill frame, so the soundscape lands at
arbitrary offsets against the fire grid. The producer wants explosion SFX
deferred to the next 16th note of the current tempo, giving kills a rhythmic
accent without changing what the player sees.

## Users

- **Player:** hears kills land on the beat, reinforcing the game's pulse and
  making combat feel more musical.
- **Developer / designer tuning feel:** can adjust the quantisation (16th note,
  tempo/BPM) and the per-tick audio cap through existing config/constants in
  one place, with tests guarding the timing contract.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, when I destroy an enemy the boom lands on the next 16th note
  of the current tempo, so a burst of kills reads as a rhythmic accent rather
  than random noise.
- As a **player**, my ship's destruction sound is beat-aligned too, but nothing
  about the explosion is delayed visually — I still see the kill instantly.
- As a **developer**, I can change the tempo through the existing rules config
  (`beatBpm`) and the explosion schedule follows it automatically, in both the
  game and every gym.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 16th-note delay helper:** A pure helper derives the delay to the next
  16th note from the shared beat clock — 16th note = `beatPeriodMs(bpm) / 4`
  (187.5 ms at the default 80 BPM) — returning `0` when the request is already
  on a tick and a finite value for an invalid/zero/negative tempo (falling back
  to `DEFAULT_BPM`, never a negative delay). Unit-tested.
- **AC2 — Non-weapon explosion cues quantised:** `playDestructionSound`
  (enemy/asteroid), `playDiverDestructionSound` and
  `playPlayerDestructionSound` are scheduled onto the next 16th note via the
  shared playback `delay` option. For a request at game-time `t`, the scheduled
  audio delay equals `next16th(t) - t` (asserted with a recording provider /
  spy).
- **AC3 — Weapon and interception cues unchanged:** The Mortar detonation cue
  and the Nova/Mortar/Arc fire cues keep firing immediately (weapons already
  fire on exact beat subdivisions), and `playBulletDestructionSound` stays
  immediate. A test asserts no beat delay is applied to these cues.
- **AC4 — Accent with a per-tick cap:** Several explosions requested inside one
  16th-note window all land on that same tick (one rhythmic accent), bounded by
  a small per-tick limiter/cap (tunable constant) so a mass kill cannot clip
  the mix. Both the accent and the cap are unit-tested.
- **AC5 — Audio-only and gym↔game parity:** Particle bursts, AOE detonation
  graphics and camera juice still spawn on the death frame — only the cue is
  deferred. The quantisation is implemented **once** in the shared core/audio
  seam and consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym; the
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard passes
  with no divergent copy.
- **AC6 — Pause/reset/tempo safety:** A frozen scene (beat clock not advanced)
  requests no cues and leaks no scheduled audio; a scene restart
  (`beatClock.reset()`) re-derives the schedule after the grid returns to
  origin; an invalid tempo still produces a valid, bounded delay.
- **AC7 — Testing/validation coverage:** New or extended tests exercise the
  helper maths (on-tick clamp, mid-window snap, invalid tempo), the scheduled
  delay for each in-scope cue, the weapon/interception exclusions, the per-tick
  cap and the VFX-unchanged path.
- **AC8 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments and the relevant GDD/audio docs
  (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3/§4, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
  where the cue behaviour is described). (CHANGELOG.md is out of scope — owned
  by the ship release pipeline.)
- **AC9 — Full suite:** Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **The beat stays silent:** no audible metronome and no background music
  (GDD §7.3); this changes cue *timing* only.
- **Game-time vs audio-clock:** the beat clock is anchored in game time, while
  playback schedules against `AudioContext.currentTime`. The delay must be
  derived from the game-time distance to the tick (`nextTick − now`), not a
  wall-clock read.
- **No new audio context:** reuse the existing shared provider/playback layer;
  every cue still degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests (no `AudioContext`
  never throws).
- **Gym↔game parity:** the behaviour lives once in the shared core/audio seam
  (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/audio/effects.ts`, `src/utils/beat.ts`) and is
  consumed unchanged by `PlayScene` and every `src/scenes/gym/` scene
  (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1).
- **UK English** in all comments and documentation.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — pure, configurable beat module: `beatPeriodMs(bpm)`,
  `beatSubdivisionMs(subdivisions, bpm)`, `nextTick`, `shotTimeFor`,
  `isOnGrid`, and `createBeatClock({ bpm, anchorMs })`. Default `80 BPM`
  (750 ms/beat). A 16th note is therefore `750 / 4 = 187.5 ms`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — owns the single `beatClock` (created
  from `loadRules().beatBpm`), exposed via `getBeatClock()`; advanced only
  through `_autoFire`/`Player.tryFire`, so a paused scene pauses the clock.
- `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts` — `SfxPlayOptions.delay` (seconds from
  `context.currentTime`) is already honoured by `play()`.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playCue(cue, options)` is the single dispatch; the
  destruction cues currently pass **no** delay:
  `playDestructionSound()`, `playDiverDestructionSound()`,
  `playPlayerDestructionSound(volumeScale)`.
- Kill seams that play those cues: `CombatScene.finaliseEnemyKill()`
  (generic/diver via `enemy.playDestructionAudio?()`), `PlayScene`'s
  `playDestructionAudio()` seam and direct calls, `GymFormationScene`, and
  `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` (`playPlayerDestructionSound`).
- Precedent for scheduled explosion cues already exists: the victory fireworks
  (`playVictoryExplosionSound({ delay, volume })`) schedule each cue against its
  visual burst in `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure helper (in `src/utils/beat.ts` or the audio layer) that returns
   the milliseconds/seconds to the next 16th-note tick for the current tempo.
2. Thread the scene's shared beat clock into the non-weapon explosion cue
   dispatch so the delay is passed through the existing `SfxPlayOptions.delay`
   channel — implemented once in the shared core/audio seam so the game and
   every gym behave identically.
3. Add a small per-tick cap for simultaneously-queued explosion cues.
4. Keep every weapon cue, the bullet-interception cue and all explosion VFX
   immediate.
5. Update the relevant docs and code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — Add the 16th-note delay helper (and/or a shared
  `nextSubdivisionDelayMs`), with JSDoc and edge-case handling.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Accept/derive a beat delay for the in-scope
  destruction cues; add the per-tick cap.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Pass the beat-clock-derived delay at
  `finaliseEnemyKill()` (the shared kill seam), keeping parity.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — Expose/consume the shared beat clock
  for the audio schedule.
- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` — Route the player-death cue through the shared
  beat-aware dispatch (called by `PlayScene` / `GymFormationScene`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Update the destruction-audio call sites if the
  delay must be supplied by the caller.
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` / `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — Only if
  the cue behaviour description changes (no new recipes expected).
- Tests: `src/utils/beat.test.ts`, `src/audio/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the scene/gym audio
  tests.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption A1 — scope ("everything except weapons"):** quantise the
  non-weapon destruction booms (`playDestructionSound`,
  `playDiverDestructionSound`, `playPlayerDestructionSound`). Weapon cues
  (Mortar detonation, Nova/Mortar/Arc fire) are excluded because weapons
  already fire on exact beat subdivisions. `playBulletDestructionSound`
  (interception feedback) is also excluded.
- **Assumption A2 — victory fireworks out of scope:** the end-of-run victory
  explosions already schedule their cues explicitly against their visual
  bursts (`spawnVictoryFireworks`); adding a 16th-note quantisation would
  desync audio from those visuals. Treated as out of scope; recorded for
  producer confirmation.
- **Assumption A3 — swarm burst out of scope:** `playSwarmBurstSound` is an
  enemy-volley whoosh, not an explosion; left unchanged.
- **Risk R1 — audio/game clock skew:** if the audio context is suspended or the
  scene is paused, a fixed game-time delay could land late on resume. Mitigation:
  schedule from the game-time delta, clamp the maximum delay to one 16th note,
  and assert the no-cue-when-frozen path.
- **Risk R2 — clipping from stacked accents:** a mass kill can queue many cues
  onto one tick. Mitigation: the AC4 per-tick cap (documented, tested,
  tunable).
- **Risk R3 — parity drift:** computing the delay at only one call site would
  leave the game/gym behaviour divergent and trip the duplicate-body guard.
  Mitigation: one shared seam, enforced by AC5.
- **Risk R4 — scope creep:** applying the same treatment to enemy fire cues or
  other SFX is out of scope; record any such opportunity as a linked
  `discovered-from:` work item rather than folding it in.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUZQ33GR006AKXD** – Core: pure actionIntensity computation + config (completed)
- **AH-0MUWYQRML000FLMT** – Document audio capture and costs (completed)
- **AH-0MUGY8HHU006XMU9** – Run full test suite and fix any failures (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: beat, called, current, delay, explosion (+10 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: beat, called, current, delay, explosion (+10 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: called, current, explosion, land, next (+5 more)

**Manual cross-references**

- **AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B** — "Bullets from the players ship should always fall on
  the beat" (completed): the silent 80 BPM fire grid this item builds on; the
  beat clock in `src/utils/beat.ts` and `CombatCoreScene.beatClock` are its
  outputs.
- **AH-0MUGPSOVM006Z1OJ** — "Implement pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock
  module" (completed): the helper this change extends.
- **AH-0MUGY84L1004H2UP** — "Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable
  via existing config plumbing" (completed): `beatBpm` in `src/core/rules.ts`
  is the tempo source the delay must follow.
- **AH-0MUGQCMNA0061J4A** — "Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with
  phase-locked beat scheduling" (completed): the phase-lock precedent.
- **AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V** — "Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and
  player deaths" (completed): the visual explosion layer deliberately left
  immediate by this item (Assumption A2/Q2=A).
- **AH-0MUJS85X0006EXGV** — "Major-explosion voice limiter" (completed):
  prior art for capping stacked explosion audio (AC4).
- **AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A** — "Dedicated player-destruction SFX" (completed):
  owns `playPlayerDestructionSound`, one of the in-scope cues.
- **AH-0MTVYC6E8005YN6F** — "Divers need SFX" (completed) and
  **AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG** — "Diver has no audio" (completed): own
  `playDiverDestructionSound`, another in-scope cue.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which explosion cues are quantised to the next 16th note?** —
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): "Everything except weapons, which have
  their own synchronization pattern." → Scope is the non-weapon destruction
  booms: `playDestructionSound`, `playDiverDestructionSound`,
  `playPlayerDestructionSound`. Weapon cues (Mortar detonation, Nova/Mortar/Arc
  fire) stay immediate because the weapon fire grid already synchronises them.
- **Q2 — Do the visual explosions move with the audio, or only the sound?** —
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): "A" → Audio only; all explosion VFX
  (particle bursts, AOE detonation graphics, camera juice) stays on the death
  frame.
- **Q3 — How should several explosions requested inside one 16th-note window
  behave?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): "A" → Accent/stack: every
  queued cue lands on the same next tick, with a small per-tick limiter/cap to
  protect the mix.
- **Assumption A2 (recorded, not a question):** victory-firework explosions are
  out of scope because they already schedule against their visual bursts.
- **Assumption A3 (recorded, not a question):** `playSwarmBurstSound` is a
  volley cue, not an explosion, and is left unchanged.

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.
